newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Laura Ashley sees recovery delayed.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Laura Ashley sees recovery delayed.

text.p: British fashion group Laura Ashley Holdings Plc, warning of sharply reduced profits, said on Tuesday its turnaround would be delayed by this year's disappointing results.

Chief executive Ann Iverson, citing infrastructure problems and losses in the U.S., said the firm's recovery would take longer than the three-to-four year period she predicted when she was hired in 1995.

"Clearly this year is going to be disappointing, but once we correct the problems that we've identified, I think we will get back into the turnaround. So it has been delayed," she told Reuters in an interview.
Iverson predicted a first-half pretax loss of 4.5 million stg -- including a 1.0 million stg charge -- followed by a return to profit in the second half and breakeven figures for the full year.
Those estimates represented sharp markdowns from the company's strong year-ago pretax profits, which totalled about 5.2 million stg in the first half and 16.2 million stg for the year to January 25.
To help staunch U.S. losses, American-born Iverson said Laura Ashley would cut back its new store openings there until existing stores' performance improved.
The company planned to open 13 stores in the U.S. this year.
"We're not going to open any next year until we get these new stores up to speed, which I know is absolutely going to happen," Iverson said.
Despite current setbacks, Iverson said she still viewed the U.S. as a major opportunity for expansion.
"The potential of the U.S. remains extremely high," she said, adding that she planned to continue her current turnaround strategy for the overall company.
"When you see the problems, or more importantly the scale of them, the first port of call is to take action, and that's clearly what we're doing," she said.
Those actions included plans to close two factories in Wales -- where the firm was founded in the 1950s -- resulting in a first-half charge of 1.0 million stg and about 190 job cuts.
Contrary to recent press speculation that her own days at Laura Ashley may be numbered, Iverson said she had no plans to leave the company.
When asked whether she planned to stay, she said, "Absolutely. I am still very committed, and I look forward to bringing the potential of the brand to fruition."
Laura Ashley's shares stayed little changed, rising 1.5p to about 58p at 0930 GMT.
